content.value_statement: Metabase frontend changes need consistent TypeScript review. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code check standards, tests, accessibility, performance, security, bundle size, and analytics.
actual_capabilities: Reviews TypeScript and JavaScript diffs against Metabase frontend standards.
Prioritizes no explicit or implicit any in new code.
Checks readability, maintainability, and appropriate test coverage.
Flags accessibility, performance, security, bundle size, and analytics gaps.
Uses Metabase-specific guidance for React, Redux, and frontend review patterns.
limitations: It depends on Metabase guidance files outside the skill directory.
It is tailored to Metabase conventions, not generic TypeScript projects.
It does not replace compiler, linter, or test suite results.
It needs enough diff and repository context to assess behavior correctly.

use_cases.title: Pull Request Review
use_cases.description: Review a TypeScript or JavaScript pull request before requesting human approval.

use_cases.title: Standards Enforcement
use_cases.description: Find Metabase coding standard violations before a change reaches team review.

use_cases.title: Review Training
use_cases.description: Help new contributors learn which frontend issues Metabase reviewers expect them to catch.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Diff Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript diff with the Metabase TypeScript review skill. Focus on correctness, style, and clear next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Frontend Quality Pass
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this frontend change for Metabase standards. Include accessibility, performance, test coverage, and analytics questions where relevant.

prompt_templates.title: Blocking Issue Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pull request for blocking TypeScript issues. Prioritize no explicit or implicit any, type modeling, and unsafe null handling.

prompt_templates.title: Full Release Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a larger feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this feature branch as a Metabase frontend reviewer. Rank findings by severity and separate blockers from advisory improvements.

output_examples.input: A React modal diff that adds icon-only buttons and no focus handling.
output: Blocking: Add accessible names to icon-only controls.
High: Confirm the modal traps focus and restores focus after close.
Question: Should this user-facing flow emit an analytics event?

output_examples.input: A TypeScript service diff that introduces broad object types and missing tests.
output: Blocking: Replace broad types with a narrower domain model.
Medium: Add tests for null and undefined response cases.
Advisory: Rename intermediate values to clarify the transformation path.

output_examples.input: A frontend route diff that imports a large utility module at route load time.
output: High: Check whether this import increases the initial route bundle.
Medium: Consider a narrower import or lazy loading path.
Question: Is this dependency already used on the same route?

best_practices: Provide the full diff and relevant surrounding files before asking for review.
Run local type checks and tests before using the skill for final review.
Ask for severity-ranked findings when preparing a pull request summary.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill as the only source of truth for compiler correctness.
Do not ask for generic TypeScript advice without Metabase repository context.
Do not ignore accessibility, analytics, or bundle size findings because they are not type errors.

faq.question: What code does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews TypeScript and JavaScript changes, especially Metabase frontend pull requests and diffs.

faq.question: Does it enforce Metabase standards?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on Metabase TypeScript, frontend, React, Redux, and review expectations described by the skill.

faq.question: Can it find accessibility issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks reviewers to flag keyboard support, focus management, labels, ARIA names, and semantic interaction issues.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can ask for test coverage, but separate tools must run the compiler, linter, and test suite.

faq.question: Is it useful outside Metabase?
faq.answer: It may help with general frontend review, but its rules are written for Metabase conventions.

faq.question: What context should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the diff, related files, test results, and any product behavior that affects the review.
